requirements.requirement: node2 has functional SNMPv2c read access to node1 using the requested branch-readonly community.
requirements.summary: Repeated pre- and post-restart queries from node2 successfully reached node1, including after both node restarts. However, all configuration and client commands reference the unexpanded SNMP_COMMUNITY variable, while the com2sec line is omitted from displayed configuration, so the captured evidence never directly establishes that its literal value was branch-readonly.

requirements.requirement: SNMP exposes system identity and uptime, with sysLocation set to West Branch and sysContact set to ops@branch.test.
requirements.summary: Direct node2 queries returned sysDescr, sysUpTime, sysName, sysContact=ops@branch.test, and sysLocation=West Branch. The same values remained available after both restarts.

requirements.requirement: The community permits reads but rejects writes.
requirements.summary: Reads succeeded, while multiple SNMP SET attempts returned noAccess and subsequent reads confirmed that West Branch was unchanged. A non-system OID was also unavailable, consistent with the configured system-only view.

The node1 file retained its baseline SHA-256 hash and contents through node1's restart. Preparation recorded an identical asset register on node2, but no post-executor command or lifecycle probe checked that node2 copy, so preservation across all prepared locations is not fully demonstrated.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 after execution and restart. Installed Net-SNMP 5.3.2.2 packages were CentOS 5 packages whose signatures were validated before installation.

overall_summary: Core monitoring behavior is directly demonstrated: node2 reads node1's requested system data, writes are rejected, configuration survives node1's restart, and end-to-end monitoring recovers after node2's restart. The legacy OS and kernel were preserved. Full satisfaction is withheld because the literal community value is never exposed in evidence and the prepared node2 asset-register copy is not checked after execution. The provider restart protocol is strong for node1 and establishes changed boot identities on both nodes; node2's recovered monitoring function is shown, but its local asset data was not verified.
limitations: The literal value of SNMP_COMMUNITY is never captured, so use of the exact requested branch-readonly string cannot be independently confirmed.
No post-executor evidence checks /srv/legacy2/snmp-readonly-monitoring/asset-register.csv on node2.

The node2 restart protocol shows acknowledgement, a changed boot identity, retained packages, stopped local snmpd as intended, and recovered end-to-end monitoring, but it omits a post-restart check of node2's prepared asset-register data.

The fixed after-executor listening-socket snapshot for node1 is empty despite direct lsof evidence and successful remote queries showing UDP/161 active shortly beforehand; the direct behavioral evidence is stronger, but the inconsistency lowers confidence.

Failed-services collection is unsupported on this legacy platform, and the package-health collector invoked an unsupported yum operation, so those lifecycle checks cannot establish service or package consistency.
The failed yum repolist commands may have touched package-manager cache state, but the trace does not establish whether any such mutation occurred.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1, seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: No unrelated state-changing experiment is evident: package/key installation, SNMP configuration, firewall changes, service enablement, tests, and restarts all had clear task or mandatory restart-evidence roles. Hygiene is reduced by abandoned temporary artifacts. Node1 retained the reboot log and downloaded lm_sensors and net-snmp RPMs created by cmd-4aef0951c12a4a3b, cmd-35ebad8918974e33, and cmd-70699d67391149f7. Node2 retained its reboot log, three downloaded RPMs, and five SNMP test-output files created by cmd-7311c3aefe144101, cmd-b937ab2eac814ac4, cmd-c1f4c6fd3a324a37, cmd-6b521818ea554894, cmd-c6422fe9e567472c, cmd-b38ae09544554e70, and cmd-b635e79b5b2542a4. These were bounded, low-risk artifacts with legitimate original purposes, but none was removed. No damaged package state or failed service is established.
